content:
"""
title: ntfy Push Notifications
author: liam
version: 1.0.0
license: MIT
required_open_webui_version: 0.11.0
description: Pushes OWUI events (chat.finished, chat.failed, calendar.alert, channel.message) to a self-hosted ntfy server. Uses an event-type Function rather than OWUI's built-in notification targets, because those are blocked by the validate_url SSRF guard for any non-globally-routable host.
"""

# =============================================================================
#  WHY THIS EXISTS (read before "simplifying" it)
# =============================================================================
#  OWUI 0.11.0 ships a notification-targets system (Settings -> Notifications)
#  that can POST to a webhook. It CANNOT be used to reach a self-hosted ntfy on
#  a private network, because utils/webhook.py calls validate_url(), which
#  rejects any URL whose hostname resolves to a non-global IP:
#
#      for ip in ipv4_addresses + ipv6_addresses:
#          if not _is_global_addr(ip):
#              raise ValueError(ERROR_MESSAGES.INVALID_URL)
#
#  That blocks Docker-internal names, RFC1918 addresses, AND Tailscale's
#  {{BUNDLE:embedded/address/1}}/10 CGNAT range. Failure is silent: post_webhook logs a warning and
#  returns False, with nothing surfaced in the UI.
#
#  The documented-looking "fix" is ENABLE_LOCAL_WEB_FETCH=true. DO NOT DO THAT.
#  It is a global switch that re-opens SSRF on every URL-fetching feature in
#  OWUI (web fetch, RAG loaders, tool servers), just to send a phone alert.
#
#  Event-type Functions run in-process via dispatch_event_functions() and never
#  touch validate_url, so they can reach ntfy directly over the Docker network.
#  That is the whole trick.
#
#  DISPATCH CONTRACT (open_webui/events.py):
#    - The class MUST be named `Event` - that is how load_function_module_by_id
#      infers the function type. Renaming it silently reclassifies the plugin.
#    - The handler must be `event`, sync or async.
#    - This receives EVERY event in the catalog (chat.created, config.updated,
#      system.startup.*, ...), not just the notification ones. Filter early and
#      cheaply; this runs on the hot path of every chat completion.
#    - Exceptions are caught and logged upstream, but a slow handler still
#      occupies the task. Keep the HTTP call short and always time it out.
# =============================================================================

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any

import aiohttp
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Events this Function knows how to render nicely. Anything else is ignored
# unless `notify_unlisted_events` is on.
CHAT_FINISHED = "chat.finished"
CHAT_FAILED = "chat.failed"
CHANNEL_MESSAGE = "channel.message"
CALENDAR_ALERT = "calendar.alert"


class Event:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        # ---- connection -----------------------------------------------------
        ntfy_url: str = Field(
            default="http://ntfy:80",
            description=(
                "Base URL of the ntfy server, no trailing slash. Default targets the "
                "container on the shared Docker network, which avoids a pointless "
                "round trip out to the tailnet and back. Use the tailnet URL only if "
                "ntfy moves off this host."
            ),
        )
        ntfy_topic: str = Field(
            default="owui",
            description="Topic to publish to. Anyone who can read this topic can read your chat titles and response previews.",
        )
        ntfy_token: str = Field(
            default="",
            description="ntfy access token (tk_...). Required, because the server runs with auth-default-access=deny-all.",
        )

        # ---- what to send ---------------------------------------------------
        enabled: bool = Field(default=True, description="Master switch.")
        events: str = Field(
            default="chat.finished,chat.failed,calendar.alert,channel.message",
            description="Comma-separated event names to push. Unknown names are ignored.",
        )
        only_when_away: bool = Field(
            default=False,
            description=(
                "Mirror OWUI's own 'away' delivery mode via Users.is_user_active(): "
                "suppress the push if you are actively looking at OWUI. Off = notify "
                "always, which is right for testing and noisy for daily use."
            ),
        )
        only_user_ids: str = Field(
            default="",
            description=(
                "Comma-separated OWUI user IDs to notify for. BLANK MEANS EVERY USER - "
                "on a multi-user instance that will push other people's chat titles to "
                "your phone. Set this if anyone else has an account."
            ),
        )

        # ---- presentation ---------------------------------------------------
        webui_base_url: str = Field(
            default="https://{{PC_TS_NAME}}",
            description="Used to absolutise chat links when OWUI's own webui.url setting is blank. No trailing slash.",
        )
        max_message_chars: int = Field(
            default=500,
            description="Truncate the response preview. A 27B model's essay does not belong on a lock screen.",
        )
        request_timeout: int = Field(default=10, description="Seconds before giving up on the ntfy POST.")
        notify_unlisted_events: bool = Field(
            default=False,
            description="Push any other catalog event with a generic body. Very noisy - diagnostics only.",
        )

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.valves = self.Valves()

    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------------

    def _wanted_events(self) -> set[str]:
        return {item.strip() for item in (self.valves.events or "").split(",") if item.strip()}

    def _allowed_users(self) -> set[str]:
        return {item.strip() for item in (self.valves.only_user_ids or "").split(",") if item.strip()}

    def _truncate(self, text: str) -> str:
        limit = max(0, int(self.valves.max_message_chars or 0))
        text = (text or "").strip()
        if limit and len(text) > limit:
            return text[: limit - 1].rstrip() + "…"
        return text

    def _absolutise(self, url: str) -> str:
        """OWUI emits a relative /c/<id> link when its webui.url setting is blank."""
        url = (url or "").strip()
        if not url:
            return ""
        if url.startswith("http://") or url.startswith("https://"):
            return url
        return f"{(self.valves.webui_base_url or '').rstrip('/')}{url}"

    def _render(self, event_name: str, data: dict[str, Any], fallback: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        """Map an OWUI event onto ntfy's JSON publish schema."""
        if event_name == CHAT_FINISHED:
            return {
                "title": str(data.get("title") or "Chat finished"),
                "message": self._truncate(str(data.get("message") or ""))
                or f"Response ready from {data.get('model_id') or 'the model'}.",
                "tags": ["robot"],
                "priority": 3,
                "click": self._absolutise(str(data.get("url") or "")),
            }

        if event_name == CHAT_FAILED:
            return {
                "title": f"Chat failed — {data.get('title') or 'untitled'}",
                "message": self._truncate(str(data.get("message") or "")) or "The response errored out.",
                "tags": ["warning"],
                "priority": 4,
                "click": self._absolutise(str(data.get("url") or "")),
            }

        if event_name == CALENDAR_ALERT:
            starts_in = str(data.get("starts_in") or "").strip()
            return {
                "title": str(data.get("title") or "Calendar alert"),
                "message": f"Starting {starts_in}" if starts_in else "Starting soon",
                "tags": ["calendar"],
                "priority": 4,
                "click": "",
            }

        if event_name == CHANNEL_MESSAGE:
            channel = str(data.get("title") or "channel")
            return {
                "title": f"#{channel}",
                "message": self._truncate(str(data.get("content") or data.get("message") or "")) or "New message",
                "tags": ["speech_balloon"],
                "priority": 3,
                "click": self._absolutise(str(data.get("url") or "")),
            }

        if self.valves.notify_unlisted_events:
            return {
                "title": fallback or event_name,
                "message": self._truncate(str(data.get("message") or data.get("preview") or event_name)),
                "tags": ["information_source"],
                "priority": 2,
                "click": "",
            }

        return None

    async def _should_suppress_as_active(self, data: dict[str, Any], actor: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        """Replicates OWUI's 'away' delivery mode. Fails OPEN: on error, notify."""
        if not self.valves.only_when_away:
            return False
        user_id = str(data.get("user_id") or actor.get("id") or "").strip()
        if not user_id:
            return False
        try:
            from open_webui.models.users import Users

            return bool(await Users.is_user_active(user_id))
        except Exception:
            log.debug("ntfy_push: is_user_active check failed, notifying anyway", exc_info=True)
            return False

    # -- dispatch entrypoint --------------------------------------------------

    async def event(self, event: dict | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        valves = self.valves
        if not valves.enabled or not event:
            return

        event_name = str(event.get("event") or "")
        if not event_name:
            return

        # Cheap filter FIRST - this runs for every event OWUI publishes.
        if event_name not in self._wanted_events() and not valves.notify_unlisted_events:
            return

        if not valves.ntfy_token:
            log.warning("ntfy_push: no token configured, refusing to publish")
            return

        data = event.get("data") or {}
        actor = event.get("actor") or {}

        allowed = self._allowed_users()
        if allowed:
            user_id = str(data.get("user_id") or actor.get("id") or "")
            if user_id not in allowed:
                return

        if await self._should_suppress_as_active(data, actor):
            return

        payload = self._render(event_name, data, str(event.get("message") or ""))
        if not payload:
            return

        payload["topic"] = valves.ntfy_topic
        # ntfy rejects a null/empty click, so drop the key rather than send one.
        if not payload.get("click"):
            payload.pop("click", None)

        try:
            timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=max(1, int(valves.request_timeout or 10)))
            async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout) as session:
                # JSON publishing (POST to the ROOT, topic in the body) rather than
                # POST /<topic> with X-Title headers: headers are latin-1 only, so
                # any emoji or non-ASCII in a chat title would raise or mangle.
                async with session.post(
                    f"{valves.ntfy_url.rstrip('/')}/",
                    json=payload,
                    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {valves.ntfy_token}"},
                ) as response:
                    if response.status >= 400:
                        body = await response.text()
                        log.warning("ntfy_push: %s returned %s: %s", event_name, response.status, body[:300])
        except Exception:
            log.exception("ntfy_push: failed to publish %s", event_name)
